title: Assessment of hydrogen storage by physisorption in porous materials
material_description: AT 470335 | commercial activated carbon supplied by Adsor-Tech GmbH (Germany); measured after degassing at 423 K under vacuum
source_location: main-04.png (p. 8297), Fig. 2a, series AT 470335 (open squares), marker at 0.43 MPa
notes: archive: fig2a_AT470335.json; digitized 0.4329 MPa stored in bar. Fig. 2a is monochrome with overlapping series: marker assigned to its series by symbol shape, located by least-squares fit of a synthetic marker template, its ink recoloured on a copy of the page, centre extracted with digitize_figure.py markers mode (see log.md). isotherm_point_count = markers that could be counted separately; markers below about 1 MPa merge with other series along the y axis and could not be counted (see log.md). Table 1: A_BET from N2 sorption at 77 K (BET range not stated); V_P by the Gurvich rule, V_micro by the Dubinin-Radushkevich plot (pore_volume_method gives the micropore method), d_P by BJH. Table 2: packing (tap) density from a graduated cylinder, mean of at least 10 measurements; skeletal density stored as 1/(helium specific volume 0.455 cm3 g-1 printed). Degassing: 423 K printed (stored as 149.85 C), vacuum p < 3 Pa (stored as 3 Pa, an upper bound), at least 10 h. Sample amount 0.5 to 5 g (range only). Isotherms 'reversible and repeatable within <1%' (relative; no wt% value). Magnetic suspension balance from Rubotherm (Germany), model not named; buoyancy correction not stated.
basis_evidence: 'The excess capacity, which is a true experimental variable for describing equilibrium gas adsorption on a solid adsorbent, refers to the amount of hydrogen present in the adsorbed layer in excess of the bulk gas density. The absolute amount adsorbed ... is considered as the excess adsorbed amount plus the amount occupying a volume that has the same density as the bulk gas density.' (p. 8295); Fig. 2 caption: 'Excess adsorbed amounts of hydrogen at 77 K as a function of the pressure.'
material_identity: Adsor-Tech GmbH (Germany), AT 470335
